**Reduction.** Since (x²+y²)/(x+y) = (x+y) − 2xy/(x+y), and with z = 9 − (x+y) we have xy = 14 − z(x+y), set w = x+y. Then xy/(x+y) = w − 9 + 14/w, so the expression equals

E = 36 − 28·S, where S = 1/(x+y) + 1/(y+z) + 1/(z+x).

Minimizing E means maximizing S.

**Express S in terms of r = xyz.**
Π(9−x) = 729 − 81·9 + 9·14 − r = 126 − r.
Σ(9−x)(9−y) = 243 − 9·18 + 14 = 95.
So S = 95/(126 − r), which is increasing in r. We need the maximum r = xyz.

**Maximize r.** x, y, z are the roots of u³ − 9u² + 14u − r, which has three real roots only if r lies between the local min and local max of g(u) = u³ − 9u² + 14u. Critical points: 3u² − 18u + 14 = 0, u = 3 ± √39/3. The maximum r is g at the smaller critical point t = 3 − √39/3 (≈0.918), which gives roots t, t, 9 − 2t ≈ 7.16, all positive.

Using t² = 6t − 14/3: g(t) = −(26/3)t + 14 = −12 + 26√39/9 ≈ 6.04.

**Value.**
S_max = 95/(138 − 26√39/9) = 855/(1242 − 26√39).
Rationalizing (1242² − 676·39 = 1516200) gives S_max = 3(1242 + 26√39)·95/(190·95)… more directly, 28·S_max = (3726 + 78√39)/190.

E_min = 36 − (3726 + 78√39)/190 = (3114 − 78√39)/190 = (1557 − 39√39)/95 ≈ 13.83.

Numerical check: 36 − 28·95/(126 − 6.04) ≈ 36 − 22.17 ≈ 13.83. ✓
